To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Steam turbine thermal performance condition monitoring can be done using permanent plant controls and instrumentation, with results comparable to those from specialist high accuracy testing.
The Valves Wide Open (VWO) test, using permanent plant instrumentation, can be used to monitor the condition of the steam turbine, and to detect the effects of changes in condition.
the use of plant instrumentation for condition monitoring can be effective, but that a number of issues must be addressed to ensure that the results are reliable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new methodology to monitor and evaluate the condition of the steam turbine.
the development of a new approach for the performance monitoring of large-scale industrial plants.

developing a new methodology for the performance monitoring and diagnostics of steam turbine generators (STGs) based on the analysis of the steam temperature and pressure data measured at the inlet and exit of the turbine stages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the turbine is in good condition, with no significant degradation of steam path components since the previous test.

the plant instrumentation and controls system is capable of detecting significant steam path condition changes and that the results can be used to guide the timing of major outages for inspection and maintenance.

• the performance analysis method described in this paper is useful for assessing turbine condition and the effect on performance • the method can be applied to data from the plant's own instrumentation system, with the proviso that the data is of sufficient quality, and the data is taken in the right way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the plant's instrumentation systems were capable of detecting significant changes in turbine steam path conditions and that the results from these systems compared favourably with the more accurate results obtained during the Valves Wide Closed tests.
it is not necessary to conduct a high accuracy test for every condition monitoring test.
the turbine is in good mechanical condition, and that the steam path is in good condition with only minor losses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to obtain a good indication of turbine steam path condition from plant instrumentation systems.
the plant's instrumentation systems can be used to monitor the condition of the turbine and the plant, if the data is interpreted with the help of specialist services.
the plant's permanent instrumentation can provide useful results for monitoring and condition evaluation if the data acquisition is sufficiently well controlled and the analysis sufficiently refined.
